---
title: "Getting started with bmeas"
---

bmeas separates model preparation, execution planning and explicit fitting.
This tutorial prepares a small Gaussian measurement model. The displayed code
is not evaluated during website builds; it has been checked separately using
`fit = FALSE` without native compilation or sampling.

## Install the development snapshot

There is no stable GitHub Release or CRAN distribution yet. R 4.1.0 or later is
required. Install the current experimental branch:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
remotes::install_github("chenyu-psy/bmeas", ref = "work/current-0.0.47.9000")
```

## Prepare a measurement model

The formula declares one factor measured by three observed variables. Preparation
uses the Gaussian response model for these wide-format variables. This tiny data
set illustrates the interface; it is not an adequate scientific analysis.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(bmeas)

data <- data.frame(
  person = 1:4,
  x1 = c(.2, .8, .3, 1),
  x2 = c(.7, .6, -.3, .1),
  x3 = c(-.2, .6, .9, .4)
)

spec <- bmeas(bmf(G = ~ x1 + x2 + x3), data,
              subject = "person", fit = FALSE)
check_model(spec)
get_prior(spec)
```

`check_model()` exposes support and qualification boundaries. `get_prior()`
reports the resolved priors; a displayed prior is not proof of scientific
adequacy. Consult the model-specific documentation and review the implied
measurement assumptions before fitting.

## Inspect an execution plan

Fitting requires an explicit finite resource policy. Planning remains separate
from fitting and does not compile or sample:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
policy <- list(max_output_bytes = 256 * 1024^2, cache = "deferred")
plan <- execution_plan(spec, chains = 1, iter = 100, warmup = 50,
                       cores = 1, threads = 1, resources = policy)
plan
```

These settings demonstrate the planning interface. They do not prescribe an
adequate number of iterations or guarantee memory use, convergence or validity.
No fitting command is run in this tutorial.

## Where to go next

Use the API reference for `bmeas()`, `bmf()`, `execution_plan()` and
`fit_checks()`. The [development guides](https://github.com/chenyu-psy/bmeas/tree/work/current-0.0.47.9000/docs)
describe supported computation profiles, explicit posterior-consumer budgets,
predictive checks and structural postprocessing. Formal Bayes factors and
density MCSE remain unavailable.
